name: Datacenter hall
pitch: 2 MW of servers for your clients. Needs power to run.
whyItMatters: More capacity serves more clients, and every MW of servers needs more MW of power behind it.

name: Gas power plant
pitch: 6 MW, steady, cheap to build. Burns gas.
whyItMatters: Gas is reliable and compact, but every MWh emits around half a tonne of CO2 over its life cycle.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for gas combined cycle: 490 gCO2e/kWh

name: Coal power plant
pitch: 10 MW, the cheapest power per MWh. Also the dirtiest.
whyItMatters: Coal packs a lot of power on little land, at the highest carbon and air-pollution cost of any source.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for coal: 820 gCO2e/kWh

name: Biomass plant
pitch: 5 MW from burning wood. Sounds green.
whyItMatters: Burning wood emits CO2 now; regrowing forests take decades to absorb it. Whether it is green depends on where the wood comes from.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for dedicated biomass: 230 gCO2e/kWh (highly debated)

name: Wind farm
pitch: 9 MW of turbines. Delivers about a third of that, when the wind blows.
whyItMatters: Wind is clean and cheap to run, but it needs a lot of land per MW and it does not blow on demand.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for onshore wind: 11 gCO2e/kWh; capacity factor ~25-40 %

name: Solar farm
pitch: 12 MW of panels. Delivers a sixth of that on average. Better in the south.
whyItMatters: Solar is clean and cheap to run, but only works by day: a sunny site produces twice as much as a northern one.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for utility solar PV: 48 gCO2e/kWh; capacity factor ~10-25 %

name: Hydro dam
pitch: Big, clean, steady power from the river. The valley floods.
whyItMatters: Hydro is low-carbon and dependable, but a dam floods land, blocks fish and changes the river for everyone downstream.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, life-cycle median for hydropower: 24 gCO2e/kWh
